common.noNetworkTitle: This computer is on no network
common.noNetworkText: No search was made at all: this computer has no network connection. To search, it has to be on the same network as the projector — by cable or Wi-Fi.
common.noNetworkHint: Check the network connection, then search again.

errors.undefinedCommand: The projector does not know this command.
errors.outOfParameter: The projector did not accept this setting.
errors.unavailableTime: Not possible right now — the projector is busy, for instance warming up or cooling down.
errors.projectorFailure: The projector reports a fault with itself.
errors.authorizationFailed: The password is wrong. You can change it behind the gear icon.
errors.replyMismatch: The projector gave an unexpected answer.
errors.malformedResponse: The projector's answer could not be understood.
errors.notConnected: No connection to the projector at the moment.
errors.connectionTimeout: The projector did not answer in time.
errors.notConfirmed: The projector did not confirm the command. Take a quick look at the screen — often it worked anyway.
errors.generic: The projector did not carry out the command.

operate.muteCoupledHint: This projector can only mute picture and sound together. That is why there is one switch here instead of two — it always takes both.
operate.muteCombinedHint: This projector can only hide the picture together with the sound. "Mute sound" switches the sound alone.
operate.muteCombinedAudioHint: This projector can only hide the picture together with the sound. "Mute sound" switches the sound alone – but only while the picture is showing.
operate.volumeHint: The projector does not report a volume level — all you can do here is step it up and down.
operate.noSources: No picture source has been set up yet. You can catch up on that behind the gear icon in the top right.
operate.powerOffConfirmText: After being switched off, the projector needs a few minutes before it can be switched on again.
operate.connectingText: The app is contacting the projector.
operate.connectingRetryText_one: The projector is not answering straight away. The app will try once more.
operate.connectingRetryText_other: The projector is not answering straight away. The app will try {{count}} more times.
operate.offlineText: The app keeps trying. If nothing changes, this usually helps: switch the projector on or check the network cable. Everything else is behind the gear icon in the top right.
operate.connectionShaky: The projector is not answering right now – the app keeps trying.
operate.poweringOnTitle: The projector is being switched on …
operate.poweringOnText: Please be patient — starting up usually takes half a minute to a minute.
operate.poweringOffTitle: The projector is being switched off …
operate.poweringOffText: The lamp will cool down afterwards.
operate.warmingText: This usually takes half a minute to a minute.
operate.coolingText: While the lamp cools down, it cannot be switched on again.
operate.videoMutedTitle: The screen is blank right now
operate.videoMutedText: The projector is still running — only the picture is hidden.

tech.passwordLabel: Password (if one is set on the projector)
tech.standbyHint: The search only finds projectors that are currently answering on their network port. A projector that is switched off usually shuts down its network card as well. For it to stay reachable in standby — and to let you switch it on from here — the projector menu must have "Network standby" (sometimes "LAN in standby" or "Always On") enabled under Network.
tech.deviceStandard: No device profile – the PJLink standard applies.
tech.deviceLearned: No device profile. Learned in use: the picture can only be hidden together with the sound.
tech.noInputsYet: No inputs known yet. The button below asks the projector.
tech.reloadInputs: Read the inputs from the projector again
tech.class2Unknown: Not known yet — the app asks for this when connecting. As soon as the connection is up, what this projector can do on top will appear here.
tech.class1Reported: This projector reports PJLink Class 1. Volume, freeze and maintenance readings belong to Class 2 and are not available on this device. Hiding the picture and muting the sound belong to Class 1 — those stay on the operating screen.
tech.class1Assumed: The projector gave no usable answer when asked which PJLink level it supports — the reason is in the activity log below. As a precaution, the Class 1 rules apply here. That does not mean this projector is really limited to Class 1: if the manual says PJLink Class 2, another connection attempt is worth trying.
tech.class2Available: This projector reports PJLink Class 2. PJLink does not reveal which of those features it actually supports — that has to be tried out. Each feature can be switched on individually here. If the projector answers on the first attempt that it does not know the command, the feature switches itself off again.

volume.title: Volume
volume.description: Buttons for louder and quieter on the operating screen. PJLink only knows steps up and down here — the projector does not hand out a current level, so no slider can be shown.

freeze.title: Freeze picture
freeze.description: Holds the picture still. Unlike "Hide picture", the screen stays bright — useful while something is being prepared on the computer.

deviceDetails.title: Serial number and software version
deviceDetails.description: Shows both here on this page. Helps when contacting the manufacturer.

inputNames.title: Input names from the projector
inputNames.description: Takes the input names stored in the projector as a suggestion for the picture sources above.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: Shows which picture is coming in and which resolution the projector recommends.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.description: Operating hours of the filter and the order numbers for the replacement lamp and filter.

tech.applyInputNames: Take the input names from the projector
tech.applyInputNamesConfirmTitle: Take the names from the projector?
tech.applyInputNamesConfirmText: The picture source names given here will be replaced by the ones stored in the projector.
tech.restartSetupConfirmText: The saved connection and the names of the picture sources will be lost.

console.heading: PJLink commands
console.intro: Sends a line to the projector exactly as typed and shows its answer. Commands take effect at once – "POWR 0" switches off without asking.

invalid.prefix: The line has to start with %.
invalid.class: The % is followed by the class: 1 or 2.
invalid.command: The command is exactly four letters or digits, e.g. AVMT.
invalid.separator: Command and parameter are separated by exactly one space.
invalid.parameter: The parameter is missing or longer than 128 characters.

reason.not-connected: Not connected to the projector – connect above under "Connection".

setup.whereText: The app searches the network for projectors. For that, the projector must be switched on or in network standby.
setup.enterIpInstead: Enter the IP address yourself instead
setup.scanDuration: This takes up to half a minute.
setup.noneFoundIntro: That usually has one of these reasons:
setup.noneFoundReasonOff: The projector is completely off. A switched-off projector usually shuts down its network card as well and is then invisible to any program. Switch it on with the remote control for the setup.
setup.noneFoundReasonStandby: For it to stay reachable while switched off, the "Network standby" setting (sometimes "LAN in standby" or "Always On") must be enabled under Network in the projector menu.
setup.noneFoundReasonPjlink: PJLink is not enabled in the projector menu.
setup.noneFoundReasonNetwork: The projector and this computer are on different networks.
setup.chooseDevice: Choose the projector you want to control.
setup.passwordHint: If a PJLink password is set on the projector, enter it here — otherwise just continue.
setup.ipRequired: Please enter an IP address first.
setup.noInputsText: The projector did not reveal its connectors. You can catch up on that later on the technical page — the controls work without it, just without a choice of picture source.
setup.nameInputsTitle: What do you call these connectors?
setup.nameInputsText: The projector reports these inputs. Give them names everyone understands — and untick everything you never use.
setup.doneText: From now on the controls show {{sources}} and the on/off switch. Everything technical lives behind the gear icon in the top right.
